title: Add UAVCAN/CAN dissector
description:
Add a dissector for the UAVCAN/CAN CAN bus protocol.
For specification see https://uavcan.org/

packet-uavcan-can implements the low-level UAVCAN/CAN transport protocol such as header parsing and packet ressembly.

packet-uavcan-dsdl implements the basic UAVCAN public_regulated_data_types messages for things such as Node id allocation, file transfer and heartbeat. In the future packet-uavcan-dsdl can be re-used for other UAVCAN transports such as UAVCAN/UDP.

So do you want the last captured byte (what you get here) or the last transmitted byte (tvb_reported_length(tvb)-1) that could miss in the capture because of a snap length. Presumably you want the latter and Wireshark would print a "packet size limited during capture" if not the frame data was captured. Presumably this is the latter.

I realize that previously you probably wanted to mark as generated the item related to this tree. In that cas the proper way of doing it would have been:
```
    can_id_tree = proto_tree_add_subtree_format(uavcan_tree, tvb, 0, 0,
                                                ett_uavcan_can, &ti, "CAN ID field: 0x%08x",
                                                can_info.id);
    proto_item_set_generated(ti);
```

as tvb_reported_length(tvb) is called multiple times in this function, I guess it would make sense to cache it in a local variable

The input parameter should be a proto_item, not a proto_tree. That's why in my previous comment I suggested to do:
```
    can_id_tree = proto_tree_add_subtree_format(uavcan_tree, tvb, 0, 0,
                                                ett_uavcan_can, &ti, "CAN ID field: 0x%08x",
                                                can_info.id);
    proto_item_set_generated(ti);
```

Okay but the protocol isn't generated by wireshark, only the can_id_tree is generated by wireshark. Would it be better just to omit this `proto_item_set_generated(ti);` instance so you get the result as shown below?

![image](/uploads/8a5efc991954b9fdb12852e48aa55735/image.png)

The CAN ID field tree is generated (when you select it no byte is highlighted). With my suggestion I would expect
```
CAN ID field: 0x907d5503
```
to be displayed as
```
[CAN ID field: 0x907d5503]
```
Note that in your proto_tree_add_subtree_format() function call I replaced NULL by &ti so as to get the proto_item corresponding to the CAN ID field text.
